To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

PD-1 is highly sensitive in the diagnosis of angiimmunoblastic Tcell lymphoma (AIT) and peripheral Tcell lymphoma unclassified (PTCU), but is not specific for these entities, because it can also stain reactive lymphoid entities.

the sensitivity of PD-1 in the diagnosis of AITCL and PTCLU is high, and that PD-1 may be expressed in reactive entities, particularly viral lymphadenitis and progressive transformation of germ centers.
PD-1 expression is a highly sensitive but not a specific marker for the diagnosis of peripheral-T cell lymphoma.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the expression of PD-1 in T-cell lymphoma and reactive lymphoid tissues.
the use of immunohistochemistry in the diagnosis of T-cell lymphomas, and specifically with the use of the PD-1 antibody in the diagnosis of AITLC and PTCLU.
the development of novel methods for the detection and characterization of lymphoid malignancies, and the identification of new markers of lymphocyte activation and differentiation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

PD-1 immunohistochemistry should be used as a confirmatory test in the diagnosis of AIT-L and PTCLU, but should be interpreted with great caution when used in isolation in the diagnosis of reactive lymphadenitis.

PD-1 immunohistochemistry is a useful ancillary tool for the diagnosis of AITT, PTCLU, and anaplastic-ALK-negative large-cell lymphomas, but it may be positive in reactive lymphoid entities, and thus should be interpreted with care.
PD-1 immunostain is a very useful tool in the diagnosis of AITCL and PTCLU.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PD-1 expression is highly sensitive for AITL and some PTCLU, but it may also be positive in a variety of reactive lymphoid proliferative processes.
PD-1 expression is a useful marker in the diagnosis and differential diagnosis of peripheral Tcell lymphomas.
PD-1 immunostaining is a highly sensitive but not specific marker for AITL and T-cell lymphoma.
The main takeaway from our work is that
PD-1 is a highly sensitive but not specific marker for AITL, and its use should be interpreted in the context of the clinical and immunophenotypical findings.

PD-1 expression is not a specific diagnostic marker for peripheral T-cell lymphoid proliferations and that its presence should be interpreted in the context of the entire clinical and histologic picture.
PD-1 positivity should not be the sole criterion for diagnosis of AITCL or PTCLU, but rather a component of a panel of markers and clinical information.
